notes: Every timed command is a fresh process; wall time includes startup and completed operation.
CPU is the harness self plus reaped child CPU during each timed command, not wall time or machine utilization.
Fixed paired rounds use deterministic shuffled method order; all samples and warmups are retained.
Tiny-file commands have 31 measured pairs; the other fixtures have seven. One warmup pair is excluded from each median.
No caches are purged. Full source/setup verification reads precede timing; larger fixtures can exceed RAM, so content is not assumed resident.
Setup, full content/mode/link verification and cleanup are outside timed commands and identical between methods.
Clone baseline uses cp -cRp to request native cloning and preserve metadata; no weaker byte-copy baseline is substituted.
Every move uses an absent exact destination on the same filesystem. Existing-destination exit-status differences are not timed.
Deletion timing ends only after process exit, and absence is checked immediately; no rename-to-trash or deferred deletion.
These commands do not promise fsync durability; this benchmark makes no durable-write or power-loss claim.
Volumes is used only for filesystem validation and cleanup protection; diskutil device inventory is not a comparison baseline.
Speedup is baseline median divided by stallionfs median; values below one retain regressions.
All workloads are generated synthetic fixtures; node_modules-shaped files are not installed third-party dependencies.
Large profile sizes use decimal GB (1,000,000,000 bytes) and MB (1,000,000 bytes); dependency files are 1,024 bytes each.
Git profile targets refer to its committed source files; .git files/bytes and actual combined totals are reported separately.
Every source byte is written. Repeated deterministic blocks are allowed; sparse files and filesystem compression are rejected.
Allocated bytes sum st_blocks * 512, including directory metadata; they are not exclusive physical usage of shared APFS extents.
Each large fixture is removed before generating the next; headroom covers source, a complete copy, metadata and two GiB reserve.
Checkpoints and full verification are outside timed commands. Partial reports remain invalid until cleanup and frozen-hash checks pass.
Optional memory rows are separate three-sample /usr/bin/time -lp child measurements; RSS and footprint are bytes, not cumulative child peaks.
Memory wrapper wall time includes extra process startup and must not be compared with unwrapped timing rows; memory rows are excluded from speedups.

comparison_method.timing: Medians exclude one warmup per method/case; all 496 rows, including 44 warmups, are retained.
comparison_method.cpu: cpu_children_s is completed-command user plus system CPU, including threads. cpu_self_s and aggregate cpu_s remain separate diagnostics; neither is substituted for command CPU.
comparison_method.cpu_diagnostics: User and system CPU medians are derived separately from measured rows. System fraction is the median of each sample's children_system_s / cpu_children_s, not the ratio of medians. A zero denominator makes that diagnostic unavailable. Total cpu_children_s remains the comparison metric.
comparison_method.cpu_utilization: Average CPU cores per command sample = cpu_children_s / wall_s; the reported value is the median of those ratios, not a ratio of medians. One core is approximately one fully occupied logical CPU over the measured interval; this is not machine-wide utilization. Lower total CPU work does not imply lower average or instantaneous load. Peak utilization is unmeasured.
comparison_method.memory: Three separate child measurements per method/case; 132 rows. Peak RSS and charged physical footprint are bytes, not unique system RAM. Observed min/max ranges are not confidence intervals. Wrapper times are excluded from timing medians.
comparison_method.formulas: Difference = StallionFS median minus Apple median; percent change = 100 * difference / Apple median; ratio = Apple median / StallionFS median. Negative differences and ratios above one favor StallionFS. Unavailable counters remain null.
comparison_method.rates: Clone/delete regular-files/s = fixture regular-file count divided by median command wall time. Includes .git regular files and excludes directories/symlinks. No file rate is reported for moves. Copy-on-write rates are not data-transfer throughput.
comparison_method.units: Times are seconds and memory is bytes. KiB/MiB are 1024/1048576 bytes; large fixture MB/GB are decimal.
comparison_method.scope: Absent exact destinations, same APFS volume, no durability flush. These measurements do not establish equivalent overwrite/cross-volume behavior or a universal filesystem gain.

export_provenance.preservation: Every original field and raw row is unchanged; only derived comparisons and this provenance are added.
export_provenance.path_sanitization: No paths were changed; export is refused if a personal local path is found.

release_applicability.scope: The final wheel changes Python interruption diagnostics to honor --json and refreshes README metadata. Native CLI operations, the scanner extension and imported workspace API modules are byte-identical to the measured package. None of the measured paths executes the Python dispatcher; file-command --version preflight uses it outside measurement. Original measurement fingerprints are retained. The revised interruption diagnostic was regression-tested, not benchmarked.
